Houston Dealer Sells 2023 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS Weissach for $211,000
21 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer/autoevolution
Can I say I'm surprised this 2023 718 Cayman GT4 RS Weissach just sold for $211,000? Not really. These cars have been commanding ridiculous sums for years now, and while prices have gone down (somewhat), in the end we're still talking about exotic supercar money for a used Cayman.
To be fair, calling this car "used" is a bit of a stretch since it only has 68 miles on the clock, and also, exotic supercars cost roughly twice nowadays what they used to cost 10 or so years ago. I think I'm still living in the past a little bit - in my head, at least.
This is also me being fair: I've made my feelings about the GT4 RS pretty clear in the past. It's a brilliant machine, and one of the finest track-focused sports cars Porsche have ever manifested into existence. I also think it's overpriced, especially when you consider what else you could buy for the money if you negotiate hard enough - like say, a Corvette with literally twice the horsepower of the Cayman.
There was a 2026 Corvette ZR1 Convertible that sold for $217,000 at auction earlier this year. Who wouldn't rather have the Vette over the 718? I know it's a GT4 RS, but it's in no way hotter than a ZR1 . Maybe as a collectible, it is. But otherwise, 9/10 people would take the Chevy, and you can't convince me otherwise.
Anyway, back to this Cayman GT4 RS and its spec, which is objectively impressive. Obviously. The Arctic Gray colorway works really well together with the Satin Black 20" forged wheels, the yellow accents, and the yellow Porsche-branded calipers. The Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes (PCCB) were optioned from the factory, as was the front-axle lift system - a must-have on any track weapon.
Other highlights include the High-Gloss Black door handles, carbon-fiber window triangles, bi-xenon headlights, and a set of Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, inside is where you'll find the carbon fiber bucket seats with black leather, Deep Sea Blue Race-Tex and Deep Sea Blue stitching trim, plus Race-Tex upholstery on the dashboard, console, and sun visors. Then there's the Bose surround-sound system, a fire extinguisher, the illuminated carbon-fiber door sill guards, Racing Yellow seat belts and door pull loops, a Race Tex-wrapped steering wheel, and the optional Light Design Package.
The latter is responsible for the LED lighting in the overhead console, door handles, door storage compartments, footwells, and vanity mirrors. Then there's the Chrono Package stopwatch, which boasts a white dial. Pretty sweet, actually.
Last but not least, the mid-mounted 4.0-liter flat-six , pushing 493 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic. Porsche would expect you to hit 60 mph (97 kph) in about 3.2 seconds behind the wheel of a GT4 RS, but independent testing showed that you can be even quicker.
